meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'стать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to stop, cease', paired with 'переставать'.

examples.text: Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

examples.text: Приезжай сейчас! Иначе я перестану давать тебе деньги!
examples.trans: Come over right now! Otherwise I'll stop giving you money!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'about', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'yesterday', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'place; seat' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to, towards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common feminine noun meaning 'truth; honestly' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to get out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'цедура'). Common feminine noun meaning 'procedure' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The procedure will take a few minutes.
Arkady Borisovich, prepare for the procedure.
